events.event: First yard shift transit and food deliveries begin.
Regional rail reaches morning freight/passenger conflict window.
Schools, offices and certification halls open; commercial power demand rises.
Port drayage peaks as overnight orbital arrivals clear customs.
Industrial canteens and retail districts peak.
Outbound container consolidation begins for evening launch slots.
Second major commuter peak overlaps yard shift change.
Heavy road movements increase as daytime restrictions ease.
Retail deliveries and municipal maintenance dominate local freight.
Market boats and aquaculture freight enter central basins.
Water transit commuter peak.
Dry Quarter customs and visitor services reach full staffing.
Biological sample and cold-chain transfers peak.
Commuter ferries and neighborhood markets peak together.
Storm-maintenance and utility crews take priority on selected channels.
Mine crews depart camps; haul roads become freight-priority.
Water, food and fuel deliveries spread from freight yard.
Claim offices, assay labs and construction suppliers open.
Inbound landers create short bursts of pad congestion.
Crew buses return; Container City food and service demand spikes.
Repair shops work late because idle equipment loses claim revenue.

rule: Daily schedules provide deterministic baseline traffic and demand; incidents and weather modify rather than replace them.
